cases.question: When is a student given a warning versus placed on probation for failed units?
cases.reference_answer: At the end of the semester, a student who fails 25% to 49% of the total academic units registered shall be warned by the Dean and advised to improve performance. A student who fails 50% to 74% of the total academic units registered shall be placed on probation for the succeeding semester, and the Dean shall reduce the load accordingly. Probation may be lifted upon passing all subjects carried during the probation term.

reference_evidence.title: Scholastic Delinquency
reference_evidence.excerpt:
4.1. Warning. At the end of the semester, A student who fails 25% to 49% of the total academic units he registered shall be warned by the Dean and advised to improve his/her performance.
4.2. Probation. At the end of the semester, A student fails 50% to 74% of the total academic units in which he registered shall be placed on probation for the succeeding semester, and the Dean con- cerned shall reduce his/her load accordingly. A student's proba- tion status may be lifted upon passing all the subjects carried dur- ing the term s/he is in probation period.

cases.reviewer_notes: Warning and probation are one section; dismissal is a separate case.

Failing more than 75% of total academic units enrolled subjects the student to dismissal from the College, except that an incomplete grade is not included in the computation of earned units, and this dismissal rule shall not apply to students who receive final grades in only nine academic units.

cases.question: How can a grade of 4.00 be removed, and what happens if an INC is not completed on time?
cases.reference_answer: A grade of 4.00 may be removed by repeating the subject or by re-examination. The highest grade obtainable upon re-examination is 3.00; failing the removal examination gives 5.00. Only one removal examination is allowed and it must be taken within one academic year or the grade becomes 5.00. If the subject is a prerequisite for the next semester, removal must be accomplished before the next enrolment. The removal fee is P20 per unit. A special removal examination may be given upon the College Dean's written-petition approval and is charged P100 per unit. If INC is not completed within the prescribed period of one year, it is automatically changed to 5.0.

cases.question: If I am a graduate student, how long can a Leave of Absence last and what if I do not file one?
cases.reference_answer: A graduate student who intends to take a leave of absence must accomplish a Leave of Absence form stating the reason and the length of time. The length of time for LOA should not exceed two (2) years and is considered part of the residency. An extension beyond the prescribed maximum residency requires one penalty subject for every year of the extension. Failure to submit a LOA would mean absence without official leave (AWOL).

reference_evidence.title: Leave of Absence (LOA)

Should there be an extension beyond the prescribed max- imum residency, the student shall take one (1) penalty subject (additional course not yet taken) for every year of the extension. Failure to submit a LOA would mean absence without official leave (AWOL)

cases.reviewer_notes: Graduate Studies article. Do not apply the two-year cap to undergraduate LOA.

cases.question: How do I apply for Honorable Dismissal, and can I be readmitted afterward?
cases.reference_answer: A student of good standing who wants to withdraw shall present a written petition to the Registrar signed by the parent or guardian. If granted, the student is given Honorable Dismissal. All indebtedness to the university must be settled before the statement is issued. A student granted Honorable Dismissal may not be readmitted in the university. A student who leaves because of suspension, dropping, or expulsion due to disciplinary action is not entitled to Honorable Dismissal.

reference_evidence.title: Honorable Dismissal

cases.question: After how many absences will I be dropped from a class?
cases.reference_answer: The Student Handbook contains two different numeric thresholds. The undergraduate Absence section says a student accumulating unexcused absences equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject shall be dropped from that subject, and time lost due to late enrolment counts as absence. The Dropping section says students shall be dropped if they have an accumulated absence of at least 25% of the total number of class hours in a semester. The graduate Attendance policy says absences equivalent to twenty percent (20%) of the total number of hour per day session for a particular subject shall cause the student to be dropped. The corpus therefore does not present a single consistent percentage for all students.

reference_evidence.title: Absence
reference_evidence.excerpt: A student accumulating unexcused absences from class, equivalent to twenty percent (25%) of the total number of hours per day session for a particular subject, shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class, as the case may be.

reference_evidence.title: Dropping
reference_evidence.excerpt: Students shall be dropped if they have an accumulated absence of at least 25% of the total number of class hours in a semester.

reference_evidence.title: Policy
reference_evidence.excerpt: A student accumulating absences from class which is equivalent to twenty percent (20%) of the total number of hour per day session for a partic- ular subject shall be dropped from the roll of students for the particular subject or class.

cases.reviewer_notes: Genuine corpus conflict, including an internal wording clash of 'twenty percent (25%)' on the undergraduate absence card versus 20% on the graduate attendance card. The reference answer reports both figures and does not pick a winner.

cases.question: What is the maximum course load for a graduate student in a regular semester?
cases.reference_answer: Under Graduate Studies course load rules, a student’s maximum load is nine (9) units per semester and not more than six (6) units if the subject has a laboratory during the summer weekend session.

reference_evidence.title: Course Load
reference_evidence.excerpt: A student’s maximum load is nine (9) units per semester and not more than six (6) units if the subject has a laboratory during the summer weekend session.

cases.reviewer_notes: Do not apply this nine-unit cap to undergraduate normal load.

cases.question: As a returning college student, how do I enlist subjects and get my Certificate of Registration?
cases.reference_answer: On the Enrollment card, old college students log in to the Student Web Portal and enlist subjects. New and old college students log in to the student portal to view the Certificate of Registration, and Registrar’s staff issues the COR. College students who are not qualified for Free Higher Education, and some other listed groups, proceed to the Office of the Registrar to claim the COR.

cases.question: What is the campus Wi-Fi password for students?
cases.reviewer_notes: The extract has no wifi password. A wifi mention exists only in remote-learning context, not as a credential or access procedure.

cases.question: Does the campus shuttle run on Sundays for students living in off-campus dorms?
cases.reviewer_notes: No shuttle schedule exists in the extract. Student Housing text only refers to a list of acceptable student dormitories and that housing should be safe, clean, affordable, and conducive to learning.

cases.question: How much does it cost to replace a lost student ID?
cases.reviewer_notes: ID processing and ID validation cards exist, but the extract does not state a lost-ID replacement procedure or replacement fee.

cases.question: What time does the university library open and close on weekdays?
cases.reviewer_notes: Library reference and circulation services are documented, but opening and closing hours are not.
